notes.text: Zachary Bolduc is out (upper body injury), reported after he played in their last game. He is a top-six forward.
Chris Kreider is out (lower body injury) and has missed the last 3 games.
Josh Anderson is out about 3-4 weeks (lower body injury) and has missed the last 2 games.
Mike Matheson is out about 3-4 weeks (lower body injury) and has missed the last 3 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Alexandre Carrier has taken his spot beside Kaiden Guhle.
Brett Berard was added to the roster on Nov 16 and has played beside Oliver Kapanen and Owen Beck.
Oliver Kapanen is no longer killing penalties: 1% of the team’s shorthanded time in 15 games, down from 33% last season.

story.head: Best vs. best
paras: The Hurricanes won the teams’ first meeting this season, 6-4 in Montréal on Oct 6. The Hurricanes have won four straight, the last a 5-1 rout of Seattle. The Canadiens (13-5-4) beat New Jersey 3-2 last night. Two of the league’s best teams meet. Going in, the Canadiens are third in the Atlantic (tied for fourth in the NHL) and the Hurricanes first in the Metropolitan (third).
The Canadiens’ record (.682) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.543), largely thanks to their goaltending. The Hurricanes’ record (.810) is about what their chances are worth.

The Canadiens get into more chippy games than almost anyone (2nd) and have had some of the best goaltending in the league (4th), but take more penalties than they draw (29th). On the other side, the Hurricanes take away shots from the point (lowest) and create more chances on the penalty kill than anyone (1st). They also keep shots away better than anyone (1st), and something has to give when the Canadiens’ shooting runs into their defense. Carolina has scored 4.14 goals a game, the most in the league, and allowed 2.19, the fewest. The Hurricanes’ power play (5th) could do real damage against the Habs’ penalty kill (23rd).

Lane Hutson (3 G / 19 A / 22 P in 22 GP) leads the Canadiens in scoring, and Cole Caufield (12 G / 7 A / 19 P in 22 GP) has a team-high twelve goals, tied for tenth in the NHL. Sebastian Aho (12 G / 17 A / 29 P in 21 GP) leads the Hurricanes in scoring and is tied for tenth in the NHL, with eight points in his last five games. Andrei Svechnikov (11 G / 10 A / 21 P in 21 GP) is next in line, with seven points in his last five games and eight goals in ten games against Montréal since 2023-24.

Jakub Dobeš (3-3-2 / .851 SV% in 8 GS) has had a rough start to the season for Montréal, but is expected to start. Pyotr Kochetkov (12-1-0 / .920 SV% in 13 GS) has been a rock in net for Carolina and is expected to start.
At home, Rod Brind'Amour likes to send Martinook, Staal and Jarvis out against opponents’ second lines, so watch for them against Bolduc, Danault and Texier.

items.text: The Canadiens are newly without Zachary Bolduc, Chris Kreider, Josh Anderson and Mike Matheson, and have been without Samuel Montembeault since Oct 6. Jakub Dobeš is expected to start. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Avalanche and the Mammoth are missing more right now.
Nick Suzuki has a point in five straight games against Carolina.
Mark Jankowski is set to play his 500th NHL game.
Juraj Slafkovský has two goals on chances worth about 7.9 goals, well below what his finishing usually turns chances into. If the chances keep coming, so should the goals.
